summary: Discovery with HarbourPoint to understand inference needs for a customer-facing summarization product. Primary concerns: 99th-p latency, cost, data residency/PHI, and time-to-first-token (TTFT). Discussed hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs, free credits quickstart, and next steps for a POC bench run.
topics: hosted vs dedicated vs VPC/private tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-09-23
- Time: 16:00 PT / 19:00 ET
- Duration: 38 minutes
- Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Mateo Alvarez (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (CTO, HarbourPoint), Samir Patel (Infra Lead), Ruth Delgado (Data Science Lead)

Auto-summary (brief): Discussed whether HarbourPoint should start with Redwood hosted API for fast time-to-first-token (TTFT) and credits, or plan for Dedicated/Private for predictable latency and compliance. Agreed on POC benchmarks and docs to share.

[00:00] Ava Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for taking time. I'm Ava from Redwood Inference, AE on the West coast. With me is Mateo, our solutions engineer. Could folks do quick intros?
[00:14] Lena Ortiz: Hi, I'm Lena, CTO at HarbourPoint. We build a doc-summarization feature for our client portal. Trying to figure out how to move from batch sidecars to real-time inference.
[00:26] Samir Patel: Samir here, infra lead. We run most stuff on GCP, some Kubernetes, a couple of on-prem racks for legacy. Latency and cost are our big blockers, and we need to keep certain data in our VPC.
[00:38] Ruth Delgado: Ruth, DS lead. We own the prompt engineering and evaluation. We have an eval suite and a prompt set, want to avoid regressions.

[00:50] Mateo Alvarez: Great, thanks. Quick framing: Redwood offers Hosted API for fastest time-to-first-token (TTFT) and quick start credits, Dedicated for reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput, and Private (VPC or on-prem) for data residency and compliance. We'll go through fit questions and then propose next steps.

[01:12] Lena: Sounds good. High level — our current infra does in-house models, MPT / slightly modified open weights, on GCP. We see 99th percentiles spiking to 800-1200ms for long docs and costs are pretty high. We want something that keeps slowness under 300ms 99th ideally, or at least predictable.

[01:42] Samir: To add, we have to keep data that includes PHI and financial identifiers within our VPC per compliance. SOC2 is in progress, ISO maybe next quarter. So VPC connectivity or Private deploy is a requirement for production for some flows. For prototyping internal tools, hosted is ok.

[02:10] Ava: Totally reasonable. Quick question — what volume are we talking? Tokens per day, or RPS?

[02:18] Ruth: For now it's low — maybe 50 reqs/min at peak for beta, average shorter sequences maybe 600 tokens, but we'll run longer summaries up to 2k tokens occasionally. The evaluation suite also runs heavy nightly jobs.

[02:36] Mateo: Good context. For 2k token tails we usually look at model choice, quantization, batching, and KV/prefix caching. On Redwood hosted we can recommend model variants with performance profiles. On Dedicated you get pinned GPU pools so latency SLOs are easier.

[02:58] Lena: If we start hosted with your self-serve API, what's typical TTFT? We need a path to first call within a day or two — SMS to stakeholders, you know.

[03:10] Ava: Yes — our PLG quickstart is designed for that. With free credits we can provision an account and you can invoke within hours. We have SDKs and docs; Mateo can walk through a minimal sample. Mate o? (laughs)
[03:26] Mateo: Sure. The typical flow is: sign up, get API key, run sample client, then import your prompt and run evals. For most customers TTFT is < 2 hours if you have a simple request ready. If you want a secure VPC tunnel for private data it takes additional network steps — usually a day or two with infra support.

[03:50] Samir: That aligns. We're interested in quickstart for dev teams, but production must be in our VPC or Dedicated with encryption. Do you support customer-managed KMS/HSM?
[04:02] Ava: Yes, Private deployments can integrate with KMS/HSM. For Dedicated we support encryption at rest and transit; keys can be customer-managed on some configs. We'll share the KMS integration patterns and the checklist.

[04:18] Ruth: Regarding quality — we need to keep model outputs stable. Do you provide eval hooks or regression alerts?

[04:26] Mateo: Redwood Optimize provides quality monitoring and can trigger regression alerts tied to prompt sets. We can tie that into your CI so you get notifications. For the POC bench we usually run your prompt set and compare outputs across model variants.

[04:44] Lena: Pricing — roughly, how do hosted vs Dedicated unit economics compare? I know you can't give a line-item without usage profile but do you have rule-of-thumb?

[04:54] Ava: Rule of thumb: hosted is best for early/variable usage because you pay per token; Dedicated is cost-effective at steady high throughput with reserved contracts. We can send a tailored matrix. For heavy long-context summarization, batching and KV cache on Dedicated can reduce per-token cost substantially.

[05:18] Samir: Any cold-starts or that KV cache — we heard some runtimes have big cold latencies. How does Redwood handle KV cache warmup?

[05:26] Mateo: We do automatic prefix/KV caching and continuous batching. For workloads with repeated contexts (like similar document types) cache hit rates can dramatically reduce latency on subsequent token generations. We'll include expected numbers in the benchmark plan; but initial first call sometimes pays the cold penalty.

[05:50] Lena: Okay can you run a bench that mirrors our traffic? We want p50/p95/p99 numbers.

[05:58] Mateo: Yes — ideal is you provide a small sample traffic profile and a few prompt examples. We'll run a 1-hour bench on hosted and on Dedicated variants if you want, and share latency and cost breakdowns per token.

[06:12] Ruth: One more constraints — audit logs and traceability for regulated customers. Do you expose token-level logs and per-route dashboards?

[06:22] Ava: Redwood Console offers token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-model dashboards, tracing hooks, and audit logs. For Private or Dedicated we can extend retention and SSO integration for your enterprise.

[06:36] Samir: About network — for VPC we prefer private link style or VPC peering; do you do AWS PrivateLink equivalents for GCP?

[06:44] Mateo: We support VPC integration options for major clouds — on GCP it's VPC-SC and private service connect patterns. We'll send the specific networking doc; setup is usually an infra sync and a few firewall rules.

[07:00] Lena: Any gotchas with headers or tool-calling? We have downstream systems and might need function calls from responses.

[07:08] Mateo: We support function/tool calling and structured outputs. There are best practices for validating tool outputs — we'll include an example pattern.

[07:20] (brief crosstalk)
[07:28] Samir: Our timeline — we want a POC in 3 weeks, production in 3 months if results look good. Does that timeline seem reasonable?
[07:36] Ava: Absolutely. Quickstart + bench this week, pilot next week, Dedicated sizing in parallel. For production in 3 months that's a common path: start hosted, run pilot, then either lift to Dedicated or Private depending on compliance.

[07:54] Lena: If we start hosted and then move to Dedicated later, how invasive is that migration?

[08:02] Mateo: The API surface is consistent across modes, so the integration code rarely changes. The big work is rollout: model pinning, traffic routing, and possibly tokens/keys rotation. We help with canary rollouts and fallback policies.

[08:18] Ruth: For evaluation, we'll want an apples-to-apples quality comparison: same prompts, same seed, same model variant if possible. How deterministic are outputs across your hosted vs Dedicated?

[08:30] Mateo: Outputs should be consistent if you pin model versions. There can be minor differences if different hardware or quantization profiles are used. We'll document the model variants and quantization levels so you can compare.

[08:46] Lena: Security docs — we need SOC 2, ISO, data flow diagrams. Can you share redacted diagrams?

[08:54] Ava: Yes, we'll share SOC2 and ISO attestations, a data flow diagram, and the VPC deployment checklist. We'll also include the compliance contacts on our side.

[09:06] Samir: One nit: do you support customer-managed ingress filtering? We want to ensure only our subnets can hit the endpoints.

[09:14] Mateo: Yes, with Private deployments and VPC peering you can restrict by subnets and use IAM + SSO for auth. We'll include the network ACL pattern in the doc.

[09:28] (pause)
[09:35] Lena: OK let's talk concrete next steps.
[09:38] Ava: Proposed next steps: 1) Ava to send pricing + Dedicated options and SOC2 + ISO one-pagers; 2) Mateo to draft a bench plan and tooling checklist; 3) HarbourPoint to send sample payloads and prompt set; 4) schedule 1-hour bench for week of Sep 29. Agree?

[09:56] Ruth: Yes. And can you seed our account with credits so our engineers can TTFT?

[10:02] Ava: Absolutely. We'll issue free credits and include quickstart instructions. That should get you to first call within a few hours for dev.

[10:12] Samir: On the POC bench, can Redwood run both hosted and Dedicated variants or do we need a committed contract for Dedicated bench?

[10:20] Mateo: We can run a short Dedicated bench in most cases without a full commit — we have short-term reserved capacity for benching. We'll note that in the plan.

[10:30] (background noise, brief mute)
[10:44] Lena: Any known competitors or pitfalls we should watch for?

[10:50] Ava: Competitors like Anthropic or OpenAI have similar hosted APIs but don't always offer the same Dedicated/Private multi-mode with tooling. Some infra vendors offer self-hosted runtimes but then you handle the orchestration; Redwood tries to provide both the runtime and the orchestration in managed or private forms.

[11:10] Ruth: Good. Small thing — do you capture logs at token level by default or is that opt-in? We need to avoid storing sensitive tokens.

[11:18] Mateo: Logging is configurable. For PHI flows you can disable token retention and use on-device or VPC deployment with customer-controlled retention. We'll include the settings.

[11:32] Ava: Ok I think we have enough to action. Quick recap: we'll send pricing and security docs, seed credits, and plan a bench run. Who's the owner for sending the payloads?

[11:44] Samir: I'll own the sample payloads and traffic profile. Ruth will own prompt set and SLO targets.

[11:50] Ava: Great — we'll follow up with calendar invites. Anything else?

[11:56] Lena: No, that's it. Thanks.

[12:00] (meeting closes)

Post-meeting notes (auto-generated):
- Action items agreed.
- Bench plan to include p50/p95/p99 latency, per-token cost, and cache-hit experiments.
- Security pack (SOC2/ISO + network checklist) will be delivered with VPC patterns.

Questions (captured):
- Q: Can Redwood run a Dedicated bench without full commit? A: Yes, short reserved bench capacity usually possible.
- Q: How quickly can we TTFT with hosted? A: Under a few hours with quickstart + credits; VPC adds 1-2 days config.
